ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-acceptance and continuous screening of all directors, officers, shareholders and UBOs against the Canadian Consolidated Autonomous Sanctions List, Special Economic Measures Act schedules, Criminal Code terrorist entity listings, UN Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List, and any additional domestic or supranational PEP databases. Politically exposed persons (foreign and domestic) must be identified, risk-rated, and subject to enhanced due diligence, source-of-funds verification, and senior management approval before incorporation proceeds. FINTRAC reporting obligations and record-keeping rules under the PCMLTFA must be integrated into the corporate onboarding and ongoing monitoring framework.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Alberta Corporate Registry (Service Alberta) — name search and reservation through authorized Registry Agents and the official Alberta corporate registry system
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must use the Latin alphabet and may include numerals and typographical symbols. English and French names are accepted; a name in any other language must be transliterated into English and, if necessary, accompanied by a certified English translation. The name must not be merely descriptive, deceptive, or likely to be confused with an existing corporate, trade, or intellectual-property name in Alberta.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the incorporator should first request written reasons from the Registrar. If the name is refused for confusion, descriptiveness, or offensiveness, the incorporator may alter the name and submit a new name search/reservation. If the initial refusal concerns a reserved or protected word, prior ministerial or industry-regulator approval may be obtained and appended to the re-submission. Where the Registrar refuses under the Alberta Business Corporations Act, the applicant may apply to the Court of King's Bench of Alberta for a judicial review or directive, typically within 21 days of receiving the refusal notice, or may refer the matter to the office of the Registrar for an administrative reconsideration if the grounds are procedural or typographical.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual registered office is generally permissible for an Alberta Business Corporation if the address is supplied by a licensed corporate service provider or registered agent and is a real physical address in Alberta, not a post office box. For a low-risk EdTech subscription business with no physical inventory and no commissioned sales force, a virtual registered office is sufficient for statutory service of process and records retention. However, a virtual office does not by itself establish commercial substance for Canadian tax purposes, and CRA may examine whether the business has a place of management, employees, or other operational presence in Alberta.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low — below 5% annual probability for an unregulated EdTech subscription issuer with no physical inventory and no on-premises business activities. An unannounced on-site inspection is unlikely absent tax fraud indicators, CRA audit selection, or federal/provincial enforcement conditions.

incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Alberta imposes no minimum paid-up capital requirement for business corporations; shares may be issued for nominal consideration such as one dollar per share
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The Board of Directors of the proposed corporation resolves: (1) to subscribe for and issue 1,000 common shares at $1.00 per share for aggregate consideration of $1,000; (2) to adopt the registered office at [Insert Full Address], Calgary, Alberta; (3) to appoint [Director Name] as the first director and [Officer Name] as the first officer; and (4) to authorize preparation and filing of Articles of Incorporation with the Alberta Corporate Registry. step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Resubmit corrected application within 10 business days if queried for deficiencies

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA); primary portals are Business Registration Online (BRO), My Business Account, and Represent a Client. Alberta corporate registrations are administered separately by Alberta Corporate Registry.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A corporation carrying on business in Canada must obtain a CRA Business Number (BN) and register applicable program accounts, including an RT GST/HST account and, where applicable, an RC corporate income tax account. The applicant submits incorporation or constitutional documents, registered office and principal business information, directors and ownership details, activities, expected taxable supplies, accounting periods, and authorized representative information through CRA Business Registration Online or the prescribed non-resident registration process. A non-resident entity without a Canadian permanent establishment may register for GST/HST where it makes taxable supplies in Canada, including supplies subject to the non-resident digital-economy rules. CRA may request identity, incorporation, banking, contracts, customer, platform, and business-activity evidence. Canada does not issue a separate national VAT number distinct from the BN; the GST/HST registration number is the BN followed by the RT program identifier. A Canadian corporation generally also receives or applies for an RC corporate income tax account. Alberta does not impose a provincial sales tax.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canadian corporations are generally taxed as separate legal entities and have no U.S.-style check-the-box election. A corporation may elect specific statutory treatments where available, such as eligible capital or accounting-period elections, but these do not convert the corporation into a flow-through entity. Partnerships are generally fiscally transparent, subject to partnership and anti-avoidance rules. Canadian hybrid-mismatch rules can deny deductions or impose inclusion where arrangements exploit differences in the tax treatment of entities or instruments between Canada and another jurisdiction. A non-resident corporation remains subject to Canadian tax on income earned in Canada and may have withholding, filing, and permanent-establishment obligations under domestic law and an applicable tax treaty.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax (GST), administered federally by the Canada Revenue Agency. Alberta has no general provincial sales tax; the applicable headline consumption tax for ordinary Alberta supplies is generally GST.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 of worldwide taxable supplies, excluding zero-rated supplies, generally measured over a single calendar quarter or over four consecutive calendar quarters. Registration can be required earlier where the small-supplier threshold is exceeded or where special non-resident digital-economy rules apply. Certain public service bodies and financial institutions have different thresholds or rules.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada has no general real-time GST invoice-clearance, government e-invoicing, or mandatory digital tax-stamping regime for ordinary commercial supplies in Alberta. Registrants must issue compliant GST invoices or other documentary evidence, retain electronic books and records, and provide prescribed information when requested by CRA. Electronic records must remain reliable, complete, accessible, and auditable. Platform billing through Apple or Google does not by itself eliminate the supplier's GST obligations; the tax treatment depends on the supplier, platform, customer location, place-of-supply rules, and applicable digital-economy provisions. CRA's electronic filing and payment requirements may apply based on registrant status and filing period.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods exported from Canada may generally be zero-rated where the supplier exports or ships them outside Canada and satisfies the GST export conditions. Services supplied to non-residents may be zero-rated only where the statutory exported-service requirements are met. For services, the supplier should establish that the recipient is a non-resident, that the service is supplied to and for the use of the non-resident, and that no exclusion applies. Important exclusions and limitations can apply to services relating to real property or tangible personal property in Canada, personal services physically performed in Canada, services connected with litigation or regulatory proceedings in Canada, and certain intermediary or financial services. Digital language-learning software or subscriptions require a specific place-of-supply and customer-status analysis; customer residence, billing address, IP or geolocation evidence, app-store contractual role, payment records, and usage facts should be retained. Zero-rating does not automatically eliminate GST registration, filing, evidence, or input-tax-credit requirements.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Canada Customs export declaration or applicable electronic export reporting record, where required by the goods-export rules
Commercial invoice, purchase order, contract, and evidence identifying the non-resident customer
Bill of lading, airway bill, courier record, or other carrier documentation evidencing export from Canada, where goods are involved
Proof of delivery or receipt outside Canada, where relevant

For offshore services or digital supplies: customer residency evidence, contractual terms, billing and payment records, platform settlement statements, geolocation or account data, and evidence that statutory zero-rating conditions and exclusions were considered
Bank or payment processor records supporting receipt of consideration; an inward remittance certificate is not generally a Canadian statutory requirement
GST/HST returns, general ledger, tax invoices, credit notes, refund claims, and input-tax-credit support
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Canada generally has no statutory foreign-exchange repatriation deadline for export proceeds. CRA may reassess GST incorrectly zero-rated supplies, deny related input tax credits or refunds, and recover tax, applicable penalties, and compound daily interest. Failure to file or late filing can trigger statutory penalties; false statements or omissions may attract a penalty generally equal to the greater of CAD 100 and 25% of the understated tax or overstated credit, while gross-negligence penalties can generally equal 50% of the resulting tax or credit adjustment. Fraudulent claims may lead to criminal prosecution, fines, and imprisonment. Customs non-compliance can result in seizure, monetary penalties, reassessment of duties and taxes, and penalties under the Customs Act and related legislation. Documentation must be retained for the applicable statutory retention period, commonly at least six years after the end of the relevant year, subject to exceptions and CRA requirements.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada), established under the Bank of Canada Act (R.S.C., 1985, c. B-2); the Minister of Finance holds overall authority for official reserves (Exchange Fund Account), with OSFI supervising banks and FINTRAC administering the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains unrestricted CAD convertibility on both current and capital accounts. No exchange-control licensing, quota, or approval regime exists under the Currency Act or Financial Administration Act. Profit remittance is free, subject only to Part XIII withholding tax (25% statutory; 15% treaty dividends / 5% for qualifying corporate shareholders) and transfer-pricing documentation. Capital repatriation and liquidation distributions require no regulatory clearance, conditional on solvency and creditor-protection compliance.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Canada has imposed no mandatory surrender/conversion ratio or statutory timeline on export proceeds since 1951; exporters retain receipts in any currency in domestic or offshore accounts. Only statistical/export-reporting obligations apply (via the Canadian Online Export Reporting portal) for shipments above C$2,000 under the Export and Import Permits Act; no monetary conversion or repatriation duty attaches.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium feasibility. Canada has no standalone EMI licence; offshore digital EMIs such as Wise, Payoneer and Revolut Business may only operate as FINTRAC-registered money services businesses (post-1 June 2021 PCMLTFA regime). They are legally constrained from accepting deposits, issuing cheques or accessing LVTS, and cannot host CRA payroll or GST/HST deductions, so a Schedule I bank account remains mandatory; EMIs function as a settlement and FX overlay.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: No statutory mandate for physical attendance applies to a Canadian-owned Alberta corporation, but PCMLTFA requires verified identity of all directors and beneficial owners; Schedule I banks generally accept video-call KYC for domestic principals, while non-resident directors/UBOs trigger either an in-branch interview or notarized ID plus banker's confirmation from a recognized OECD financial institution. Remote-only opening is denied for shell-like registrations (virtual-mailbox address) or entities under 24 months old.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Aggregated Apple App Store / Google Play micro-payouts arriving as lump sums with no matching customer invoice
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Apple Developer Program and Google Play Console merchant agreements; monthly payout reports showing subscription volumes, refunds and platform tax deductions; revenue-recognition policy mapped to IFRS 15/ASC 606; treasury reconciliation trail.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership chain passing through a Delaware or other foreign intermediate holding company
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified articles/certificates of good standing from Alberta Corporate Registry and foreign registrar; full cap table and share register; signed PCMLTFA UBO declaration (25% standard); parent financial statements and funding source evidence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Early-stage injection of large equity/convertible proceeds disproportionate to the low-risk EdTech revenue profile
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board resolution approving subscription; executed subscription/SAFE/convertible documents; remitting bank statement evidencing cleared funds; SWIFT MT103 with purpose field; use-of-proceeds memo for platform build-out and licensing.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Registered office only at a corporate agent address with no physical Alberta presence
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Registry extract; executed lease or virtual-office agreement; CRA payroll account registration; remote-workforce and director contact evidence; operational narrative documenting the remote-first EdTech model.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity and intercompany loans arrive via SWIFT MT103 carrying a uniform purpose string in Field 70, e.g. 'EQUITY INJECTION / SHARE SUBSCRIPTION / ALBERTA EDTECH'; funds may be retained in USD/EUR in multi-currency accounts or converted at the receiving bank's prevailing rate. Aggregated entries above C$10,000 trigger FINTRAC reporting; values above C$25,000 require standard large-transaction records; non-resident controlling investments require an Investment Canada Act determination only above C$1.75 billion asset/EBITDA thresholds for WTO-member acquirers, inapplicable at seed/Series A size.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Domestic CAD payments clear through Payments Canada ACSS (standard ACH) or LVTS for same-day high-value; USD vendor disbursements use Fedwire/CHIPS correspondents of Canadian banks or SWIFT MT103 for offshore beneficiaries; content/licensor contracts can be supported by UCP 600 documentary letters of credit or standby LCs; royalty remittances to non-residents require Part XIII-NR6 clearance before release to avoid withholding disputes.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright deliverable FX forwards (CAD/USD, CAD/EUR, CAD/GBP) with tenors up to 24 months executed under an ISDA 2002/CSA or bank master agreement
Non-deliverable forwards referencing CAD for restricted emerging-market currencies (e.g., BRL, TRY, IDR) where physical deliverability is unavailable
Cross-currency swaps and cross-currency interest-rate swaps to match USD expenditure with CAD subscription inflows
Plain vanilla European-style FX options, collars and zero-cost structures purchased from a licensed Schedule I bank
Exchange-traded FX futures and options on the Montreal Exchange and CME for transparent price discovery at lower notionals

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Alberta Annual Return under the Business Corporations Act (Alberta)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the anniversary date of incorporation in each calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: If the annual return is not filed within the statutory window, the Registrar of Corporations may issue a notice of intent to strike; failure to remedy by the date stated in the notice results in administrative strike-off and dissolution. Reinstatement is possible only through Registrar or Court approval and payment of all applicable arrears and reinstatement fees.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal and Alberta Corporation Income Tax Returns (T2 and Alberta Corporate Tax Return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Canada Revenue Agency; Alberta Treasury Board and Finance / Alberta Tax and Revenue Administration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Six months after the end of the corporation's taxation year (fiscal year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty under the Income Tax Act is 5% of the balance of tax payable plus 1% per month for up to 12 months; late payment interest is charged on outstanding amounts. Alberta imposes parallel provincial penalties, enforcement, and possible director liability for unpaid assessed amounts.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: For a private non-offering Alberta corporation, no revenue or asset threshold automatically triggers a statutory audit. The members must appoint an auditor at each annual general meeting unless all shareholders unanimously consent to waive the appointment for that fiscal year. An offering corporation or a corporation with listed securities is required to appoint an independent auditor.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Canadian private corporations may use Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE) or International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS); IFRS is required for offering/public corporations. The selected framework must be applied consistently in annual financial statements.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Alberta's corporate registry does not currently mandate a separate annual UBO filing form. The corporation must maintain an internal register of individuals with significant control (ISC) where applicable, update it without delay upon any share transfer or ownership change, and have the directors confirm its accuracy at the annual general meeting. The Alberta Annual Return serves as an annual attestation that registered office, director, and share data are accurate as of the anniversary date.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Individuals with Significant Control (if applicable)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: $120 – $250 per year for Alberta registered office and principal address services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: $8,000 – $20,000 per year for an independent certified audit of a subscription-based EdTech corporation if an audit is not waived

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 23.0% combined (federal 15.0% + Alberta provincial 8.0%) for general business corporations; 11.0% combined (federal 9.0% + Alberta 2.0%) for Canadian-controlled private corporations (CCPCs) on the first CAD 500,000 of active business income
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Small Business Deduction (SBD) for eligible CCPCs; Scientific Research and Experimental Development (SR&ED) investment tax credits (ITC) up to 35% on qualifying Canadian research and development expenditures; 100% deduction for certain software subscriptions? Not applicable; generally, capital cost allowance (CCA) for software assets under Class 12/50; no Alberta-specific digital media tax credit in stage 6 context.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return filed electronically through the Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) NETFILE or originating software (CANTAX, Taxprep); Alberta corporate income tax is administered by the CRA under the Alberta-Canada Tax Collection Agreement, so a single T2 covers both federal and Alberta provincial tax.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; fiscal period not exceeding 53 weeks. Interim installments may be required for large corporations, but no quarterly tax return requirement.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The T2 return must be filed within 6 months after the corporation's fiscal year-end. For a December 31 year-end, the filing due date is June 30 of the following year. The balance-due payment is due 2 months after year-end generally; CCPCs eligible for the SBD have an extended balance-due date of 3 months.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, business number (BN), registered office address, jurisdiction of incorporation, provincial code (AB), and tax year start/end dates.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a Canadian corporation with non-resident shareholders, confirm the corporation's Canadian residency for tax purposes; a non-resident director is permissible but must authorize filings through the CRA's authorized representative process.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Compute net income (loss) under the Income Tax Act, including revenue from subscription fees, incurred expenses, CCA, and adjusted for non-deductible items (e.g., 50% of shareholder entertainment).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report all cross-border EdTech service revenues as Canadian-source if negotiated from Alberta; apply transfer pricing rules for payments to related foreign entities and allocable provincial income via permanent establishment rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Calculate federal and Alberta tax payable, applying the federal 15% rate and Alberta 8% general rate; apply the SBD and allocation of federal tax reduced by abatement (10%) for provincial allocation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For non-resident-directed investments, ensure the business is not a non-resident-owned investment corporation (NRO) unless the subscription activity is passive; if active EdTech business, treat as Canadian-resident operating corporation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report non-capital loss carryforward balances and carryover amounts used. Losses may be carried back 3 years and forward 20 years.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders cannot use Canadian losses directly; the corporation must restrict loss utilization if control changes under s. 249(4) and maintain continuity records.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter SR&ED federal ITC amounts, provincial credits, and unclaimed ITC carryforward balances (10-year carryforward).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the EdTech software development is performed partly overseas, allocate Canadian SR&ED expenditures based on actual Canadian payroll; clean documentation is required for CRA pre-approval.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Schedule 88 - International Disclosure (Controlled and Non-Arm's Length Transactions)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Provide details of transactions with non-resident related parties, including subscription fees, royalty/licensing, and intercompany service payments, and certify completion of Form T106.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident co-parent agreements must include the contrived shareholding? Simple guidance: report all related-party cross-border payments even below the threshold; failure to file T106 attracts CAD 100 penalties per form and CAD 2,500 for large corporations.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty under s. 162(1): 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per full month for up to 12 months. If the corporation is assessed tax of more than CAD 5,000 and the return is late, additional penalty for repeated failure may reach 10%. Interest applies on late amounts at CRA prescribed rates (compound daily). Failure to file international disclosure forms (T106) attracts CAD 100 for small corporations and CAD 2,500 for corporations with gross revenue exceeding CAD 20 million; each unfiled form is a separate offense.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% (Part XIII tax) on dividends paid or credited to a Canadian corporation's non-resident shareholders, unless reduced by an income tax treaty.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim a reduced withholding rate under a double tax agreement (DTA): (1) the non-resident payee must obtain a valid tax residency certificate (TRC) from its own tax authority; (2) the payee must complete and submit Form NR301 (or the applicable non-resident withholding form) to the Canadian payor before each payment, or alternatively the payee may file a Part XIII refund claim after withholding; (3) the payor must keep the TRC and NR301 on file to substantiate use of the reduced treaty rate. If treaty benefits are not established, withhold at the statutory 25% and remit to CRA (Form NR52).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory Part XIII withholding: 25% for royalties and 25% for interest paid to non-residents. Under the Canada-US DTA, interest from an arm's-length Canadian borrower to a US resident lender is generally exempt; other interest may attract 15%. Royalties for copyright and patent rights often attract 10% under the Canada-US treaty (with 0% for cultural/software royalties in certain defined cases). Many other treaties (e.g., UK, Germany) provide 15% for patent/copyright royalties and 0% or 15% for interest. Exemption for interest on foreign-currency corporate obligations may apply under s. 212(1)(b)(ii).

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: CAD 1,000,000 annual aggregate value of non-arm's-length cross-border transactions (purchases, sales, services, royalties, interest) triggers mandatory contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation (TP Memo 17); a consolidated group with global revenue exceeding CAD 750,000,000 for its Canadian parent or CAD 25,000,000 aggregate? Canada's Country-by-Country Report (Form RC4649) threshold is CAD 750,000,000 in consolidated group revenue.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada does not apply the United Arab Emirates-style Economic Substance Regulations (ESR). Instead, the Canada Revenue Agency invokes the General Anti-Avoidance Rule (s. 245) and treaty anti-abuse rules to prevent artificial arrangements. An Alberta EdTech corporation must maintain real operational substance (staff, management, IP ownership decisions, contractual negotiations, QRTR? no, but physical oversight in Alberta) to avoid being treated as a conduit. The corporation must also satisfy the 'business carried on in Canada' test and, for treaty claims, may be denied benefits if there is no genuine commercial rationale or functions in Canada.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Wilfully making false statements, destroying records, suppressing subscription revenue, or using undisclosed offshore bank accounts to avoid Canadian tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal fine of up to 200% of evaded tax and imprisonment up to 5 years; civil gross negligence penalty of 50% of the understated tax under s. 163(2).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are jointly and severally liable for corporate withholding tax and GST/HST remittances under s. 227.1; where tax evasion is criminal, a court may order personal forfeiture, travel restrictions, and civil restitution against directors who participated.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Entering into cross-border transaction with a related non-resident (e.g., licensing software to a controlled foreign subsidiary) at a price outside the arm's length range, without contemporaneous documentation, and resulting in an upward adjustment exceeding CAD 100,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalty equal to 10% of the transfer pricing adjustment (net of any secondary adjustment) under s. 247(3), irrespective of fraud; no penalty if the taxpayer made 'reasonable efforts' to document the pricing at filing time.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be assessed personally if they authorized the transactions and the corporation is insolvent; for gross negligence in TP reporting, directors may also be flagged in CRA's 'Name and Shame' program for egregious tax adjustments.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to file the T2 within the 6-month statutory period, or knowingly filing a materially incomplete T2, or omitting required Schedule 88/T106 disclosure.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Late filing penalty: 5% of unpaid tax + 1% per full month (up to 12 months). Knowingly making a false statement: 50% gross negligence penalty of understated tax; access to justice under the Income Tax Act to seize unregistered assets.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally liable for employer source deductions (payroll) and GST/HST net tax if the corporation fails to remit; CRA may issue notice of assessment to directors and obtain a travel ban if tax debt exceeds CAD 100,000 under s. 227.11.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using an Alberta-incorporated entity as a letterbox conduit with no employees, no premises, and no substantive management decisions, solely to access the Canada-US DTA and stream royalties/copyright payments without Canadian taxation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: CRA GAAR reassessment under s. 245; treaty benefits denied under OECD BEPS LOB provisions (where applicable); recharacterization of dividends/royalties as taxable Canadian-source income; 50% gross negligence penalty for misrepresentation of substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who cause the corporation to issue misleading statutory declarations may be criminally charged for counseling corporate fraud; civil restitution orders may pierce the corporate veil, and directors can be prohibited from leaving Canada pending tax recovery.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to maintain appropriate anti-money-laundering protocols for high-volume cross-border digital subscription payments (Apple IAP, Google Play) or allowing chargeback/refund abuse without transaction monitoring, if the company performs any activity falling under FINTRAC's reporting entity definitions (not typically an EdTech subscription, but a client-integration risk).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA), administrative monetary penalties up to CAD 1,000,000 per violation for failure to register or report; criminal penalties up to 5 years imprisonment if wilful blindness.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of a non-registered MSB can be personally fined; directors can be jailed for up to 5 years for knowingly permitting transactions with sanctioned entities; personal travel bans may be imposed for failing to cooperate.
